Tranches (b)-(c) require commercial production and 7.5-10 Moz and are not deducted.

commodity_deck.note: Gold price (US$/oz realized) x payable ounces (Moz) x total cash cost (US$/oz, by-product) x fixed costs (G&A + exploration/corp-dev + other + NTI, US$m) drive revenue and EBITDA margin in every scenario. By-product revenue ~ $130m growing to ~$175m. Spot gold US$4,216/oz at 2026-10-09 (Yahoo GC=F; 52w 3,901-5,586). Realized: FY2024 $2,384, FY2025 $3,454, Q1-26 $4,861, Q2-26 $4,483, H1-26 $4,672. Company's own 2026 royalty/NTI planning price $4,500; its long-term sensitivity price $2,500; Hope Bay sanctioned at $3,600.
commodity_deck.calibration: EBITDA = (price - cash cost) x oz - fixed. Back-test: FY2024 (2,384 - 903) x 3.46 - 650 = 4,474 vs 4,462 reported; H1-2026 (4,672 - 1,050) x 1.70 - 400 = 5,757 vs 5,748 adjusted EBITDA reported.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR from the commodity deck (gold mean-reverting to US$3,500 by 2029 then +2%/yr nominal, ounces 3.30 -> 4.20 Moz). Historical CAGRs are not usable as a forward proxy: the 5-year series spans the Kirkland Lake merger (FY2022, equity +172%, shares +79%) and the Yamana/Malartic acquisition (FY2023), and the 3-year series is dominated by gold rising from $1,797 to $3,454/oz.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 34.2% vs revenue 30.6% vs EPS 33.4% all exceed 30% and all diverge >30% from the 3.3% selected rate -- every one of them is M&A- and gold-price-driven, not organic. Flagged for review.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs computed on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 $373.3m, FY2022 $500.0m, FY2025 $4,243.3m. Owner-FCF CAGR exceeds reported-FCF CAGR (104% vs 99% 3yr) because SBC grew slower than cash flow (0.82% of revenue FY2025 vs 1.7% FY2020) -- the opposite of the usual SBC-outrunning-cash warning. FY2025 owner FCF is itself ~$0.8bn above its underlying level because of the tax-payable build (see inputs.notes).

scenario_narratives.base: Agnico's two axes are the gold price and project delivery. Base: the 2025-26 rally does not fully unwind but the market's spot price is not a mid-cycle price either -- realized gold mean-reverts from ~$4,440 in 2026 to US$3,500 by 2029 (the 2024-26 average, ~17% below spot, and roughly where management sanctioned Hope Bay at $3,600) and then tracks inflation. Barnat costs ~150 koz/yr in 2027-28 as guided and remediation lifts Malartic unit costs; Odyssey/East Gouldie, Detour Lake underground, Hope Bay and Upper Beaver deliver about the lower half of the 20-30% growth target, taking ounces from 3.30 to 4.20 Moz by 2035 at the cost of ~$3.2bn/yr capex in 2027-28. EBITDA margin compresses from ~69% to ~60% on the lower price and inflating unit costs; FCF is squeezed hardest in 2027-29 when price is falling and the build programme peaks, then expands as capex tapers toward D&A. Cash tax runs at 40% in 2026 (payable unwind) and 35% thereafter.
scenario_narratives.bull: Gold's re-rating is structural -- central-bank accumulation, de-dollarisation and real-rate expectations keep spot around US$4,300-4,500 and then flat in real terms, so the no-hedge policy delivers full price exposure for a decade. Barnat is remediated by Q4-2026 with less lost production than the 150 koz ceiling, Hope Bay reaches the top of its 400-435 koz range on schedule, and Detour and Canadian Malartic each approach ~1 Moz/yr by the early 2030s, taking group output to 4.5 Moz. Margins hold near ~69% because royalty inflation is the main cost pressure and it only rises with price; capex falls to ~12% of revenue once the three builds are complete. This is the case the current share price requires.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2025-26 gold spike proves to be a positioning-driven overshoot: ETF and central-bank demand fade as real rates stay positive and gold retraces to US$2,800-3,000 by 2028-29 -- still well above the FY2024 realized $2,384, so this is a reversion, not a collapse. With no hedges the full fall hits revenue; Barnat's redesign loses the full 150 koz/yr and Fosterville and LaRonde grades decline, holding production at ~3.2 Moz through 2028. Hope Bay and Detour underground run late and over budget into a falling price, so FCF after the build programme is thin in 2027-29 and the growth target reaches only ~3.7 Moz by the mid-2030s. EBITDA margin settles near ~49%, the level FY2023-24 cost structures delivered at $2,000-2,400 gold.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a gold miner on a through-cycle gold price, not on the price it just realized. FY2025-H1 2026 are peak-margin years: realized gold rose from $2,384 (2024) to $3,454 (2025) to $4,672 (H1-26) while total cash costs rose only from $903 to ~$1,050, so reported FCF ($4.4bn FY2025, $2.1bn H1-26) is a peak-cycle number that also carried ~$0.8bn of deferred cash tax. The house build therefore does three things the market is not doing: it mean-reverts gold to US$3,500 by 2029 (base), it runs the 2027-29 capex peak against that falling price rather than against spot, and it caps the terminal multiple at 14x FCF. On those terms the base and even the bull case sit below today's price, which is the finding: at C$270 the market is capitalising spot gold in perpetuity plus full delivery of the growth programme. Owner FCF expenses SBC (small here, ~0.6% of revenue) and strips interest income because the $3.46bn cash and the $1.16bn equity portfolio are added back in the bridge. Risk is charged once, in the probability-weighted flows, at a single 9% USD WACC.
key_risks_to_valuation: Gold price regime: every US$100/oz of long-run price is worth roughly US$0.5-0.6/share of annual FCF per 3.5 Moz (after 35% tax), so the US$3,500 mid-cycle anchor is the single assumption the whole valuation turns on -- the bull/bear range (US$2,800-4,500) spans it.

Barnat pit-wall remediation: guidance is 60-80 koz lost in H2-2026 and up to 150 koz/yr in 2027-28 pending final redesign; a longer suspension or wider instability along the Cadillac Fault would hit the base case's largest growth asset.

Execution of four concurrent builds (Hope Bay $2.4bn, Detour Lake underground, Odyssey shaft, Upper Beaver): 2025 capex already ran above guidance and 2026 was raised twice; a 20% overrun in 2027-28 is ~US$1.3bn of FCF.

Reclamation provision of US$1.5bn is not deducted in the bridge (closure spend falls beyond the horizon and the perpetuity assumes reserve replacement); treating it as debt would lower every scenario by ~US$3/share.

Equity-portfolio and CVR bridge items: the US$1.16bn investment book is marked to volatile junior-miner prices, and the Rupert CVR could pay out all three tranches (up to ~US$500m) if Ikkari is a success -- a cost that arrives only alongside a value-creating outcome not in the ounce path.
Cost-side FX: ~60% of costs are in CAD/AUD/EUR/MXN against USD revenue; the 2026 guidance assumed C$1.36 and the C$ is at 1.43 today (a tailwind), but a reversal adds ~US$30-40/oz.
Share count: management intends to buy back the Rupert dilution; if it instead issues stock for further M&A (its pattern: Kirkland Lake, Yamana, O3, Rupert), the flat count understates dilution.

Includes the ~9.9m shares issued 16-Jun-2026 for Rupert Resources (0.0401 AEM per Rupert share, $1,687m) -- genuine non-SBC issuance, already in the count, so the count is held FLAT from here. SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so no further dilution is modelled (charging both would double-count). Management intends to offset the Rupert dilution with NCIB buybacks funded by portfolio-investment sales; buybacks are value-neutral in this model.

inputs.balance_sheet_source: Q2-2026 condensed interim statements inside the 30-Jul-2026 6-K EX-99.1 (SEC accession 0001104659-26-088794), fetched from EDGAR on 2026-10-10 -- this filing is NOT yet in research/AEM.TO/Extracted and should be downloaded. Cash $3,463,957k; long-term debt $196,825k; lease obligations $34,306k current + $89,219k non-current; investments (equity securities) $1,161,559k; income taxes payable $278,144k (vs $1,226,347k at Dec-25).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x ~0.95 beta (gold equities: low market correlation, high standalone volatility) = ~9.0% cost of equity; debt is immaterial ($197m against $3.46bn cash, Fitch A- / Moody's A3) so WACC ~= CoE = 9.0%. Below the 10.5% USD house default for tech because the asset base is tier-1 jurisdiction, investment-grade and un-levered. Gold-price cyclicality and the Barnat/Hope Bay execution risk are charged ONCE, in the probability-weighted flows -- no ad-hoc premium, and the same 9.0% across all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. Reported FCF is OCF minus additions to PP&E, so IFRS-16 lease principal ($36.0m FY2025, $15.8m H1-2026) sits in financing and is NOT in the flows; lease obligations of $123.5m (30-Jun-2026) are therefore added to total_debt once. Variable lease payments ($131m) are already expensed in production costs. Lease-asset renewal is inside the sustaining-capex line.
inputs.nci_treatment: None required. Canadian Malartic is 100%-owned since Mar-2023; San Nicolas (50% Teck JV) is equity-accounted and outside the flows and the bridge.
inputs.reclamation_note: Reclamation provision $1,509m (30-Jun-2026) is NOT deducted in the bridge: closure spend falls at end of mine life, beyond the 10-year horizon, while the perpetuity assumes continuing reserve replacement (reserves grew to a record 55.4 Moz at YE2025, ~16 years at 3.4 Moz/yr). Accretion is non-cash and excluded from EBITDA. Listed as a valuation risk rather than netted.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, with the owner-fcf-adaptations (USD reporting vs CAD quote, leases as debt, matching-asset rule for the equity portfolio, risk charged once). Routed as 'operating company, cyclical' -- a gold producer's value is a stream of FCF, but the stream is a function of a commodity price at a historic high, so the forward build is driven by an explicit gold deck x ounce path x unit cost rather than by historical CAGRs (which are M&A-broken: Kirkland Lake Feb-2022, Yamana/Malartic Mar-2023). FY0 is FY2025 (revenue $11,908m at $3,454/oz realized, 3.447 Moz). FY2025 REPORTED FCF of $4,399m was flattered by a ~$0.8bn build in income taxes payable (paid $1,178m cash tax against a far larger expense; the payable then unwound as a $1.0bn working-capital outflow in H1-2026) -- so the year-1 cash tax rate is set at 40% to carry the catch-up, and last_fcf is an anchor, not the projection base. Interest income ($58.1m FY2025) stripped because the $3.46bn cash pile is added back in the bridge; net cash is ~0.74x the FCF base, below the 1x rule of thumb, but the double-count is real at any size. Price is a regular TSX close, not after-hours. Balance sheet and share count are 30-Jun-2026 (latest filed), not the Dec-2025 annual on disk. Treat the 2026 revenue growth (+24%) as locked-in by H1 realized $4,672/oz, not as a forecast.

bear.growth_note: Gold gives back most of the 2025-26 rally: $3,400 in 2027, $2,900 in 2028, $2,800 in 2029 then +2%/yr (still 17% above FY2024 realized). Barnat redesign loses the full 150 koz/yr and Fosterville/LaRonde grade decline bites (3.20 Moz 2027-28); Hope Bay and Detour underground run late and over budget (capex $3.3bn in 2027-28 against falling revenue), so the decade growth target delivers only 3.7 Moz by 2034. Unit costs rise faster (stronger CAD, inflation) with no royalty relief large enough to offset.

base.growth_note: 2026 +24% is H1 realized $4,672 plus H2 near spot ($4,200) on 3.30 Moz (low end of guidance after Barnat). 2027-28 gold reverts $3,900 -> $3,600 while Barnat costs up to 150 koz/yr; 2029 onward US$3,500 mid-cycle (the 2024-26 three-year average realized price, ~17% below spot) inflating 2%/yr from 2031, with ounces 3.50 -> 4.20 Moz as Odyssey/East Gouldie, Detour underground, Hope Bay (first gold ~2030) and Upper Beaver deliver roughly the lower half of management's 20-30% decade growth target.
base.margin_note: Total cash cost $1,090/oz in 2026 (guidance midpoint $1,070 plus Barnat remediation; Malartic re-guided to $1,260), then +2.5%/yr nominal with partial royalty relief as gold falls. Margin compresses from ~69% at $4,440 to ~60% at $3,500 -- consistent with FY2024's 54% at $2,384 and H1-2026's 72% at $4,672.
base.tax_note: 40% in 2026 carries the ~$1.0bn unwind of the Dec-2025 income-tax payable (cash taxes guided $3.4-3.6bn vs ~35% effective); 35% thereafter = guided consolidated effective rate (Canada/Mexico 35-40%, Australia 30%, Finland 20%), which includes provincial mining taxes.
base.capex_note: 2026 $3,025m = revised guidance midpoint incl. capitalized exploration and Hope Bay construction start. 2027-28 ~$3.2bn (Hope Bay ~$600-700m/yr of its $2.4bn, Detour underground, Odyssey shaft, Upper Beaver, ~$1.1bn sustaining, ~$320m capitalized exploration). Tapers to ~15% of revenue by 2033-35, roughly D&A plus reserve replacement.
base.terminal_note: Cap multiple 14x terminal FCF binds (Gordon at 9%/2.5% would be 15.8x); upper half of the 12-15x cyclical band for a tier-1-jurisdiction, A-rated senior with a 16-year reserve life, but well below where the stock trades today on peak-price FCF. Terminal growth 2.5% nominal is price inflation only -- no real volume growth is assumed in perpetuity for a depleting asset base.

bull.growth_note: Gold holds the new regime: $4,300 in 2027-28, $4,400 in 2029, then +2.5%/yr nominal (flat real at roughly today's spot). Barnat recovers faster (3.33/3.38 Moz), and the full 20-30% growth programme lands -- 4.5 Moz by 2034, Hope Bay at the top of its 400-435 koz range, Detour and Malartic each toward ~1 Moz/yr.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. The scenarios are a near-symmetric split on one macro variable -- gold at $2,800 vs $3,500 vs $4,400+ in 2029 -- after a price that has doubled in two years, and the stock's own 40% peak-to-trough drawdown in 2026 (while gold stayed above $4,000) shows the market itself treating regime risk as two-sided. Bear is lifted from 15% because the no-hedge policy transmits the whole downside to cash flow and the Barnat event shows operational risk is live, not theoretical; bull is cut from 35% because it requires both spot gold to hold indefinitely AND the entire concurrent four-project build to land on time. No going-concern, covenant or single-customer issue argues for a heavier bear than 25%: the balance sheet is A-rated with $3.3bn net cash.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
